title: Exploring the Synergistic Mechanism of AP2A2 Transcription Factor Inhibition via Molecular Modeling and Simulations as a Novel Computational Approach for Combating Breast Cancer: In Silico Interpretations.
authors: Niranjan, Vidya; Setlur, Anagha S; K, Chandrashekar; Kumkum, Sneha; Dasgupta, Sanjana; Singh, Varsha; Desai, Vrushali; Kumar, Jitendra
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子建模、对接和200ns MD模拟及MM-GBSA，筛选天然配体抑制转录因子AP2A2以阻断其与DLEC1结合，属TF-DNA互作抑制的物理模拟研究，但未直接建模TF-DNA复合物界面，深度有限。
abstract: Studies have shown that transcription factor AP2A2 (activator protein-2 alpha-2) is involved in the expression of DLEC1, a tumor suppressor gene, which, when mutated, will cause breast cancer and is thus an excellent target for breast cancer studies. Therefore, in the present research, a synergistic approach toward combating breast cancer is proposed by blocking AP2A2 factor, and allowing the cancer cells to be sensitive to anti-cancer drugs. The effect of AP2A2 on breast cancer was first understood via gene analysis from cBioPortal. AP2A2 was then modeled using RaptorX and its structure was validated from Ramachandran plots. Using all ligands from MolPort database, molecular docking was performed against AP2A2, from which the top three best docked ligands were studied for toxicity in humans using Protox-II. Once the ligands passed these tests, the best complexes were simulated at 200ns in Desmond Maestro, to comprehend their stabilities, followed by the computations of free energies of binding via Molecular mechanics- Generalized Born Solvent Accessibility method (MM-GBSA). The results showed that molecules MolPort-005-945-556 (sachharolipids), MolPort-001-741-124 (flavonoids), and MolPort-005-944-667 (lignan glycosides) with AP2A2 passed toxicity evaluation and belonged to toxicity classes 6, 5, and 5, respectively, with good docking energies. 200 ns simulations revealed stable complexes with slight conformational changes. Stability of ligands was confirmed via snapshots at every 20 ns of the trajectory. Radial distribution of these molecules against the protein revealed very slight deviation from binding pocket. Additionally, the free binding energies for these complexes were found to be - 54.93 +/- 12.982 kcal/mol, - 44.39 +/- 14.393 kcal/mol, and - 66.51 +/- 13.522 kcal/mol, respectively. A preliminary computational validation of the inability of AP2A2 to bind to DLEC1 in the presence of ligands offers beneficial insights into the potential of these ligands. Therefore, this study sheds light on the potential natural molecules that could stably block AP2A2 with least deviation and act in synergy to aid anti-cancer drugs work on breast cancer cells.
abstract_zh: 研究表明，转录因子AP2A2（激活蛋白-2α-2）参与肿瘤抑制基因DLEC1的表达，该基因突变时会导致乳腺癌，因此成为乳腺癌研究的优秀靶点。为此，本研究提出了一种协同抗击乳腺癌的方法，通过阻断AP2A2因子，使癌细胞对抗癌药物敏感。首先通过cBioPortal的基因分析了解AP2A2对乳腺癌的影响。随后使用RaptorX对AP2A2进行建模，并通过Ramachandran图验证其结构。利用MolPort数据库中的所有配体，对AP2A2进行分子对接，从中选出对接效果最好的前三种配体，并使用Protox-II评估其在人体中的毒性。配体通过这些测试后，在Desmond Maestro中进行了200ns的模拟，以理解其稳定性，随后通过分子力学-广义Born溶剂可及性方法（MM-GBSA）计算结合自由能。结果显示，与AP2A2结合的分子MolPort-005-945-556（糖脂类）、MolPort-001-741-124（黄酮类）和MolPort-005-944-667（木脂素糖苷）通过了毒性评估，分别属于毒性等级6、5和5，并具有良好的对接能量。200ns模拟揭示了稳定的复合物，伴有轻微构象变化。通过每20ns轨迹快照确认了配体的稳定性。这些分子与蛋白质的径向分布显示与结合口袋的偏差极小。此外，这些复合物的自由结合能分别为-54.93 ± 12.982 kcal/mol、-44.39 ± 14.393 kcal/mol和-66.51 ± 13.522 kcal/mol。对AP2A2在配体存在下无法与DLEC1结合的初步计算验证，为这些配体的潜力提供了有益见解。因此，本研究揭示了潜在天然分子，它们能稳定阻断AP2A2且偏差最小，并协同帮助抗癌药物作用于乳腺癌细胞。
